# Problem 4 — the `minimal` tier downloads a scene it was never given

**The defect (MEASURED, from code read):** `_layouts/default.html:40-44` assigns `minimal` to eight page types (portal, section-projects, ramblings, archives, blog, tag, page, under-construction), but `_includes/chrome-scripts.html:25-47` only branches on `none` and `embers`, so `minimal` falls through to `three-background-scene.min.js` (843 KB, `assets/js/dist/`). That bundle then fetches Dock.fbx (63 KB), Water.fbx (34 KB) and DUV.png (259 KB) it will never show, creates a `FireworkController` nobody asked for on those pages, and `assets/js/effects/scene-mode.js:49-63` hides the dock and water after the fact by graph traversal, its own header calling itself "STILL A DEMO, NOT THE END STATE" (scene-mode.js:23).

**What minimal pages pay today (MEASURED bytes, cold visit):** 843 KB bundle + 272 KB Lanterns.fbx + 356 KB of assets they never display (Dock + Water + DUV) + ~350 KB paper sheets ≈ 1.82 MB. **Frame cost:** the dock/water are already invisible and the reflection skip landed, so the only *running* waste on these pages is the fireworks: the greeting stream is always armed at top-of-page, and MEASURED, 8 shells push p95 to 33.4 ms and the portal at 4x CPU hit single frames of **99.9 ms**. Each shell is 400 particles x 10 trail copies = 4,000 vertices (`_javascript/firework-controller.js:52-55`).

---

## The conflict Rod has to call: does `minimal` keep the greeting fireworks?

Two of Rod's own decisions collide, and the fix has to pick one:

- **Reading 1 — P72, 2026-08-22:** "a scene with only lanterns, the fireflies, and post processes" (quoted at `default.html:21-23`). No fireworks on minimal. This is the *later* decision.
- **Reading 2 — 2026-08-16:** the greeting is "The permanent top-of-page GREETING … It has no off switch by design" (`_javascript/three-config.js:98-104`).

Reading 1 also kills something P72 never mentioned: **click-to-launch fireworks** (the click handler lives inside the controller, `firework-controller.js:120-130`), so the Pyrotechnician achievement could then only progress on About and Landing. The house "later decision wins" rule says default to Reading 1, but this is a visible behaviour change on eight page types, so it is Rod's word.

**In every option below the fork is one token:** the gate reads `tier === 'full'` (Reading 1) or `tier !== 'embers'` (Reading 2). All bytes and diffs are identical either way except that Option B under Reading 2 must add the FireworkController import to its second bundle.

## Option A — ONE bundle, tier branch inside (delete the minimal entry, the demo shim, and a Rollup target)

The single scene bundle reads `document.body.dataset.sceneTier` (which `default.html:71` already writes) and initialises only what the tier owns. The 404's ember-only path folds in as the `embers` branch, so `three-background-minimal.js` and `scene-mode.js` are deleted outright.

**Delete:** `_javascript/three-background-minimal.js` (99 lines), `assets/js/effects/scene-mode.js` (117 lines). **Comment refresh (docs-are-part-of-done):** `default.html:26` ("hidden by scene-mode.js") and the embers rationale at `default.html:45-58` are then stale; the `embers` assignment at line 59 itself STAYS (the bundle branches on it and the CSS scroll-lock reads it).

- **Bytes saved per page (MEASURED file sizes):** every minimal page stops fetching Dock+Water+DUV = **356 KB** (cold portal drops 1.82 MB → 1.47 MB). Bundle bytes unchanged per page, but `assets/js/dist/` sheds the 525 KB duplicate and one Rollup target. 404 cold visit costs 843 KB instead of 525 (+318 KB) but is **0 KB** warm, since it now shares the one cached bundle.
- **Cache About → portal:** same file, full cache hit; the portal fetches nothing new at all.
- **Frame saving (tied to measurements):** under Reading 1, minimal pages lose all shells: the MEASURED portal-at-4x 99.9 ms single frames and the shells' p95 33.4/max 50 contribution vanish there; steady-state avg barely moves (shells are episodic). Also removes scene-mode's 100 ms polling interval and, via the reach gate, a dead 4 s poll on the 404.
- **Visual risk: subtle.** Under Reading 1: no greeting or click fireworks on the eight minimal page types (that is the point, and it is Rod's call). Two side effects on those pages: the transient dock/water flash before scene-mode's next 100 ms poll tick can no longer happen (INFERENCE from the poll design at scene-mode.js:99-115 — an improvement), and the `?scene=` override on a minimal page can no longer *reveal* dock/water since they were never loaded (`window.__sceneTier.counts()` debug helper also goes). **Rod looks once at: portal and one projects page top-of-scroll, plus the 404.**
- **Line delta:** ~+45 in the scene entry against −99, −117, −1 and −8 elsewhere ≈ **net −180**. D5: the added branch lines each replace whole files; nothing here is a cache or guard, it is the demo shim's job moving to where the objects are created instead of after the fact.
- **Prefer when:** you want the end state scene-mode.js's own header promised, with the fewest total moving parts.

## Option B — two honest bundles (minimal learns to load Lanterns.fbx)

The old objection (CDN FBXLoader dragging a second three.js) is moot: both entries build from the same `node_modules` (`rollup.config.js:67 nodeResolve`), so `three-background-minimal.js` can `import { FBXLoader } from 'three/examples/jsm/loaders/FBXLoader.js'` like the scene entry does.

But pixel-honesty forces a bigger rewrite than the sketch implies: today's minimal *pages* show the FULL scene's look (camera z 500, 25° scroll pitch, 25 side-margin embers of size 5 — `three-background-scene.js:84-113`), while today's minimal *bundle* is the 404's look (camera z 1500, scroll-locked, 35 page-spread embers of size 8 — `three-background-minimal.js:31-77`). One bundle must carry both, so the minimal entry gains the same tier branch as Option A:

**`_javascript/three-background-minimal.js`** — rebuilt as: A's tier read (`embers` vs `minimal`), A's embers branch (current file body, verbatim), plus a minimal branch that is the scene entry's camera/spawn/scroll code minus dock, water, DUV and fireworks, with `loadLanternsFBX` added. (The code is exactly Option A's entry with the two `tier === 'full'` blocks and the `FireworkController` lines deleted — under Reading 2 the controller import comes along, +~9 KB min.)

**`_includes/chrome-scripts.html:38-47`:**

```diff
-{% elsif include.tier == 'embers' %}
+{% elsif include.tier == 'embers' or include.tier == 'minimal' %}
   <script defer src="{{ '/assets/js/dist/three-background-minimal.min.js' | relative_url }}"></script>
 {% else %}
```

`three-background-scene.js` is untouched (it now only ever serves `full`). `scene-mode.js` still deleted, reach gate still tightened, rollup unchanged.

- **Bytes (INFERENCE, must be measured after the build — READ ONLY here):** the new minimal bundle ≈ 525 KB + FBXLoader (105 KB src) + fflate (89 KB src) + NURBS chain + the extra three.js internals FBXLoader pulls, after babel+terser ≈ **650–700 KB**. Minimal pages then save ~140–190 KB of bundle *plus* the same 356 KB of asset fetches as A. Total dist grows ~150 KB and still ships **two full copies of three.js**.
- **Cache About → portal:** broken — the portal downloads its own ~680 KB bundle even though About's 843 KB is sitting in cache; a visitor crossing both directions pays ~1.5 MB of bundles where A pays 843 KB once.
- **Frame saving:** identical to A (same things stop running).
- **Visual risk:** same as A, same "Rod looks once" list.
- **Line delta:** ≈ **net −40**, but ~60 of the surviving lines are a duplicate of the scene entry's setup in a second file. D5 verdict: this is the duplication the law exists for — two files to keep in step forever, for a byte saving that only helps a visitor who lands cold on a minimal page and never visits About.
- **Prefer when:** analytics some day show most visitors enter cold on minimal pages and never touch About/Landing, making per-page bundle weight matter more than cross-page caching.

## Option C — source-gate only, no build restructure

Smallest diff: keep both bundles and all serving exactly as today; inside the scene entry, gate what minimal was never given.

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js`** — just these pieces of Option A's diff: the `tier` read (regex `full|minimal` only), `if (tier === 'full')` on `loadDockFBX` (line 35), on the Water.fbx load (line 40), and on the `FireworkController` (line 28) with the same null-handling in the updatables list and debug global. No embers branch, no import change, ~15 lines touched.

**`assets/js/effects/scene-mode.js`** — must still be deleted, not kept: with dock/water never loaded, its stop condition (`c.dock > 0 && c.water > 0`, scene-mode.js:110-113) can never be satisfied and its poll would burn the full 10 s on every minimal page — the exact failure its own comment documents for the 404.

**`_includes/chrome-scripts.html`** — drop line 62 (scene-mode) and tighten the reach gate to `== 'full'` (same two hunks as A). Rollup, the minimal entry, and the 404 are untouched.

- **Bytes:** same 356 KB per-minimal-page fetch saving as A. Does NOT touch the 318 KB bundle delta, the 525 KB dist duplicate, or the duplicate three.js; minimal pages keep downloading 843 KB to run roughly half of it.
- **Cache About → portal:** unchanged from today (shared bundle, full hit) — same as A.
- **Frame saving:** identical to A on minimal pages (MEASURED portal spikes gone under Reading 1).
- **Visual risk:** identical to A minus the 404 (404 untouched). Same "Rod looks once" note for portal/projects.
- **Line delta:** ≈ **net −105**. D5: clean, but it leaves a 99-line source file and 525 KB of build output serving one page, which is exactly the standing debt `docs/ARCHITECTURE-HANDOFF.md:787` already schedules for removal.
- **Prefer when:** you want the runtime and fetch waste gone this week with the least review surface, accepting that the bundle cleanup happens later anyway.
